info.title: NowTempMail Developer API
info.summary: Disposable mailboxes, inbound message retrieval, and server-side OTP extraction.
info.description:
A server-to-server HTTP API for creating disposable mailboxes and reading the
mail that lands in them. Every message NowTempMail receives is scanned for
verification codes on ingest, so `verificationCodes` arrives already
extracted — you do not need to regex the body yourself.

## Launch pricing

**Every paid capability is currently available to every account.** Custom and
reserved addresses, mailboxes that live longer than 24 hours, and inbound
webhooks are all enabled while checkout is being finalised, so the
`402 plan_upgrade_required` responses documented below will not occur for
those capabilities today.

Two things this does *not* change. The numeric ceilings — requests per minute
and mailboxes per day — are still enforced, because they are abuse control
rather than price discrimination. And a request above the current ceiling
still returns `402`, since the limit is real even though there is nothing to
upgrade to yet.

`GET /v1/me` reports the situation directly: `paywall.enabled` is `false`, and
`plan` shows what you actually have right now. Build against `GET /v1/me`
rather than assuming a tier — when billing goes live, that field is where the
change will show up first.

## Base URL and versioning

All paths in this document are absolute and already include the `/v1`
prefix. `/v1` is a separate surface from the unversioned first-party routes
the web app, Chrome extension and Android app use; those are not public API
and are not documented here. Nothing in `/v1` accepts a mailbox JWT, and
nothing outside `/v1` accepts a developer API key.

This document is served live at `GET /v1/openapi.json`, unauthenticated —
fetch it there if you generate a client.

## Authentication

One credential, on one header:

```
Authorization: Bearer ntm_live_<keyId>_<secret>
```

See the `apiKey` security scheme for the format and, importantly, for why
this API cannot be called from browser JavaScript.

## Errors

Every error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` document with a stable
machine-readable `code`. Branch on `code`; `detail` is prose and may be
reworded at any time. See the `Problem` schema for the full code list.

## Rate limits and quota

Two independent ceilings, both enforced per API key by a Durable Object so
the counters are exact rather than approximate:

| Ceiling | Applies to | Headers | Error on breach |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requests per minute | every `/v1` request | `X-RateLimit-*` | `rate_limit_exceeded` |
| Mailboxes per UTC day | `POST /v1/mailboxes` only | `X-Quota-*` | `quota_exceeded` |

The minute window is a fixed window, not a sliding one: `X-RateLimit-Reset`
is the epoch second at which the counter returns to zero. The daily mailbox
quota resets at 00:00 UTC.

`GET /v1/me` runs in *peek* mode — polling your own usage never consumes the
quota it reports on.

Both 429 responses carry `Retry-After` in seconds.

## Request tracing

Send `X-Request-Id` and it is echoed back and written to the server log;
omit it and one is generated (`req_<21 chars>`). It is always present as the
`requestId` member of an error body, which is the value to quote in a
support request.

## Plan gates

Four capabilities are paid features. Each one is enforced, not ignored:
asking for it on a plan that does not include it returns
`402 plan_upgrade_required` naming the offending `parameter`, so a free-tier
caller never believes a setting took effect that did not.

| Capability | Request field | Entitlement on `GET /v1/me` |
|---|---|---|
| Custom local part | `address` | `plan.customAddress` |
| Holding an address across expiry | `reserve` | `plan.reservedAddresses` |
| Mailbox lifetime beyond 24h | `ttlSeconds` | `plan.maxTtlSeconds` |
| Inbound-mail webhooks | `webhookUrl` | `plan.webhooks` |

`domain` is *not* gated — every plan may pick any active domain.

## Webhooks

Register a callback with `webhookUrl` on mailbox creation and we POST a
signed pointer to it when mail lands. See the top-level `webhooks` section
of this document for the exact body and signature scheme,
`POST /v1/webhooks/test` to rehearse it, and `webhookEndpoints` on
`GET /v1/me` for per-endpoint delivery health.

## CORS

There is none, deliberately. `/v1` emits no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`,
rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header with
`403 origin_not_allowed`, and answers `OPTIONS` on **every** `/v1` path —
routed or not — with the same `403 origin_not_allowed` rather than a
preflight or a 404. There is nothing to preflight; call this from a server.

## Caching

Every `/v1` response is `Cache-Control: no-store`, with one exception:
`GET /v1/openapi.json` is `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` because it is
identical for every caller. Everything else is per-key and must never be
shared by an intermediary cache.

get.description:
Returns the calling key's identity, its plan's limits, and live counters.

This endpoint runs the meter in peek mode: it reports the limits without
consuming any of them, so a dashboard can poll it without eating the
budget it is displaying. `usage.requestsThisMinute` therefore excludes
the call you just made.

`plan` is the live entitlement table for this key and every field in it
is enforced — see "Plan gates" in the introduction.

### Webhook health

`webhookEndpoints` lists every endpoint registered against this key,
newest first, with its delivery health. This is the **only** place the
auto-disable decision is visible: after 20 consecutive failed delivery
attempts the dispatcher sets `status: "disabled"` and stops calling the
endpoint entirely, and nothing re-enables it on its own. If deliveries
went quiet, look here first.

Any 2xx resets `consecutiveFailures` to zero. `disabledReason` is a
machine-ish string of the form
`auto_disabled_after_20_failures:<last reason>`, where the last reason
is `http_<status>`, `timeout`, `network_error`, or
`url_rejected_<guard reason>`.

The array is empty on an environment with no developer database bound.

200.description: Plan and usage for the calling key.

paywall.note: Paid capabilities are currently available to every account while checkout is being finalised. Limits will change when billing goes live.

paid.summary: A Starter key with one healthy and one disabled endpoint

get.description:
The domains currently accepting mail. Exactly one is flagged
`default: true` — the one `POST /v1/mailboxes` will pick, chosen by the
rotation logic in `DomainManager` from per-domain health and recent
usage.

The domain set is global, not per-plan: every key sees the same list.
The list can shrink or grow without notice as domains are rotated, so
resolve it at runtime rather than hard-coding a domain.

An empty `domains` array means no domain is currently marked active. In
that state mailbox creation still succeeds against a built-in fallback
domain.

post.description:
Creates a disposable mailbox and returns its address. With an empty body
you get a generated address on the current default domain — a
ten-character local part built from a word plus digits, for example
`crystal482@allogebra.com` — that lives 24 hours.

The mailbox is owned by the key that created it. Only that key can read,
list or delete it; every other key gets `404 not_found` (see
"Ownership" on the retrieval endpoints).

**This is the only endpoint that consumes daily quota.** It is the one
endpoint that can return `quota_exceeded`.

A request with no body, or with a body that is not valid JSON, is
treated as an empty object and succeeds.

### Every optional field, and what `null` means

`address`, `domain`, `ttlSeconds`, `reserve` and `webhookUrl` are all
optional. **An explicit `null` is treated exactly as "not provided"**
for every one of them: `{"address": null}` behaves identically to `{}`
and returns a generated address. It is never an error, and never a way
to clear anything. Unknown members are ignored.

Validation runs in a fixed order — `domain`, `ttlSeconds`,
`webhookUrl`, then `address` — and the first failure ends the request,
so a body with two problems reports only the first.

### `domain`

**Not plan-gated** — every plan may pick any active domain. The value is
trimmed and lowercased, then must appear in the list
`GET /v1/domains` currently returns. A non-string, or a domain that is
not active, is `422 invalid_request` with `parameter: "domain"`. Omit it
and the rotation logic picks the healthiest domain for you.

### `ttlSeconds`

Mailbox lifetime in seconds. Must be a whole number, at least `300`
(5 minutes), and no more than your plan's `maxTtlSeconds` — 86,400 on
Free, 604,800 on Starter, 2,592,000 on Scale. It is **rejected, never
silently clamped**: a caller who asked for 30 days and quietly got 24
hours would build a retry loop against mail that has already been swept.

Omit it and you get 86,400 (24 hours) on **every** plan, Scale included.
The plan ceiling is what you may *ask* for, not what you get by default.

> Status codes here are asymmetric in the current release. Any value
> that arrives as a JSON **number** and fails validation returns
> `402 plan_upgrade_required` — including values that are merely
> malformed rather than over your ceiling (`0`, `-1`, `1.5`, `120`).
> Only a non-numeric type (`"3600"`, `true`) returns
> `422 invalid_request`. Read `detail` to tell them apart; both carry
> `parameter: "ttlSeconds"`, `plan` and `maxTtlSeconds`.

### `address`

Requires `plan.customAddress` (Starter, Scale); on Free it is
`402 plan_upgrade_required`. Accepts either a bare local part
(`my-signup-test`) or a full address (`my-signup-test@allogebra.com`) —
everything from the first `@` on is discarded, so the domain actually
used is the `domain` field or the default, never whatever you wrote
after the `@`.

The local part is trimmed and lowercased, then must:

- be 3–64 characters (RFC 5321 §4.5.3.1.1 sets the upper bound);
- match `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9._-]*[a-z0-9])?$` — lowercase letters,
  digits, dot, hyphen and underscore only, starting and ending with a
  letter or digit;
- not contain `..`;
- not be reserved (below).

These rules are deliberately stricter than RFC 5321 permits. Quoted
local parts and the wider atext set are legal in the spec, are a routing
and display-spoofing hazard, and no temp-mail use needs them.

#### Reserved local parts

Around ninety names cannot be registered, for two separate reasons:

- **Impersonation** — `admin`, `administrator`, `support`, `security`,
  `billing`, `legal`, `noreply`, `verify`, `otp`, `login`,
  `nowtempmail`, `api` and similar. On our own domains these would let a
  customer send phishing that passes every authenticity check a
  recipient can perform.
- **Deliverability** — RFC 2142 requires `postmaster` and `abuse` to
  reach a real human. Handing them to a customer breaks the
  mail-operator contract and is a fast route to the domain being
  blocklisted.

The check is evasion-aware: it is applied to the local part as given,
to the part before any `+` sub-address, and to that with every `.`, `_`
and `-` stripped. So `admin`, `admin+x`, `ad-min`, `a.d.m.i.n` and
`ad_min+test` are all rejected — every one of them delivers to something
a recipient reads as "admin".

A reserved name returns **`422 invalid_request`**, not a 409, with
``detail: "`admin` is reserved and cannot be registered."``

#### Collisions

An address already live as a mailbox, and an address reserved by another
account, both return `409 address_taken` with the identical detail
``"`<address>` is not available."`` That is deliberate: distinguishing
them would turn this endpoint into a way to enumerate other customers'
held addresses.

### `reserve`

`true` holds the local part for your account beyond the mailbox's expiry
so nobody else can claim it and you can recreate the mailbox later. It
must be a real boolean: a non-boolean value — including the string
`"true"` — is rejected with `422 invalid_request` naming the parameter,
rather than silently resolving to `false`. A silent no-op here would
mean believing you had reserved an address that you had not.

- Requires `address`. `reserve: true` on its own is
  `422 invalid_request` with `parameter: "reserve"`; a generated address
  cannot be reserved.
- Counts against `plan.reservedAddresses` (Free 0, Starter 5, Scale
  100), reported live as `usage.reservedAddressesUsed` on
  `GET /v1/me`. Over the limit is `402 plan_upgrade_required` and the
  `detail` says how many you currently hold.
- A reservation outlives the mailbox and is the stronger claim: it is
  checked before the mailbox record. Release one with
  `DELETE /v1/reservations/{address}`; releasing does not delete a live
  mailbox on that address, it only gives up the claim once the mailbox
  expires.
- Two concurrent claims on the same name cannot both succeed; the loser
  gets `409 address_taken` ("That address was just taken.").

### `webhookUrl`

Requires `plan.webhooks` (Starter, Scale); on Free it is
`402 plan_upgrade_required`. Registers — or reuses — an endpoint that
receives a signed `message.received` callback for every message this
mailbox accepts. See the `webhooks` section of this document for the
body and signature scheme.

The URL must use `https`, on port 443 or 8443, with no embedded
credentials, addressed by a public multi-label DNS name: not a raw IPv4
or IPv6 literal, not `localhost`, not a `.local` / `.internal` / `.lan`
/ `.home.arpa` style suffix, and not a wildcard-DNS host such as
`nip.io` or `sslip.io`. Anything else is `422 invalid_request` with
`parameter: "webhookUrl"` and a `detail` naming the rule you broke.
This is an SSRF control, not a style preference — the same guard runs
again at delivery time.

Registering the same URL twice on one key reuses the existing endpoint
instead of creating a duplicate, so pointing many mailboxes at one URL
gives you one endpoint with one health record. The `webhookUrl` in the
response is the WHATWG-normalised form of what you sent, which may
differ from your input (a bare origin gains a trailing `/`).

Registration happens only after every other check on the request has
passed, so a request that fails validation leaves no endpoint behind.
Registration is also idempotent by URL: re-sending the same
`webhookUrl` reuses the existing endpoint rather than creating a second
one.

### Test keys

A `ntm_test_` key is metered against the Free plan limits regardless of
the account's paid plan — which also means `address`, `reserve`,
`webhookUrl` and any `ttlSeconds` above 86,400 return
`402 plan_upgrade_required` on a test key. It is *not* a data sandbox
either: mailboxes it creates are real mailboxes on real domains that
receive real mail.

429.description:
Either the per-minute request limit (`rate_limit_exceeded`) or the
daily mailbox quota (`quota_exceeded`) was hit. This is the only
endpoint that can return `quota_exceeded`.

No `X-Request-Id` response header here — read `requestId` off the
body.

value.title: Quota exceeded
value.detail: You have created 50 mailboxes today, the maximum for the Free plan. The quota resets at 00:00 UTC.

value.title: Rate limit exceeded
value.detail: You have exceeded 30 requests per minute on the Free plan.

get.description:
Expiry, message count and the timestamp of the most recent message.

### Ownership

A mailbox owned by a different key, a mailbox created by the consumer
web app (which has no owner), an expired mailbox and a mailbox that
never existed all return an identical `404 not_found`. That is
deliberate: distinguishing them would turn this endpoint into an oracle
for which addresses are live.

delete.description:
Deletes the mailbox and every message in it, including message bodies
and attachment content. Not reversible.

This is not idempotent in the strict sense: a second call returns
`404 not_found` because the mailbox record is gone.

get.description:
Message summaries, newest first, cursor-paginated.

Summaries carry `verificationCodes` — codes extracted server-side at
ingest — so a polling loop that only needs an OTP never has to fetch a
message body at all.

### Pagination

Pass `limit` (default 25, maximum 100) and, for subsequent pages, the
`nextCursor` from the previous response. When `hasMore` is `false`,
`nextCursor` is `null` and you are at the end of the list.

The cursor is an opaque base64 token. Treat it as opaque: its encoding
is not part of the contract. If the message a cursor names has since
been deleted, the cursor resolves to the end of the list and yields an
empty final page rather than silently restarting from the top. A cursor
that cannot be decoded returns `422 invalid_request` with
`parameter: "cursor"`.

Ordering is by receive time, newest first. Because new mail arrives at
the *front* of the list, a message that lands mid-pagination can be
missed by a cursor walk; for a live inbox, poll page one rather than
paginating.

### Polling

Calling this endpoint marks the mailbox as actively watched, which is
the signal the cleanup worker uses to decide an inbox is still in use.
Poll no faster than your plan's per-minute limit allows — for a Free
key that is 30 requests a minute across the whole API, so 2s is a
reasonable floor for a single mailbox and slower if you are watching
several.

withOtp.summary: One message carrying a verification code

422.description: The address is malformed, or the `cursor` could not be decoded.

value.title: Invalid request
value.detail: The `cursor` parameter is not valid.

get.description:
The full message: headers, bodies and attachment metadata.

Messages are addressed under their mailbox rather than at a top-level
`/v1/messages/{id}`. Messages are stored keyed by recipient, so a bare
message id is not addressable without a scan, and nesting makes the
ownership check structural.

`verificationCodes` here is the same extracted set the list endpoint
returns, so either endpoint is a correct source for an OTP. Fetch the
message only when you actually need the body or the attachment list.

`to` is the mailbox from the request path — it is not stored on the
message record, and it is the address this call authorised against.

delete.description:
Deletes the message and its stored body. A second call returns
`404 not_found`.

get.description:
Metadata only. The same array is present on the message itself, so this
endpoint is only worth a separate call if you already have the message
id and do not want to transfer the body.

Attachment ids are the attachment's index within the message as a
string: `"0"`, `"1"`, and so on. They are stable for the life of the
message but are not globally unique.

Streams the attachment bytes. This is the one endpoint that does not
return JSON on success.

`Content-Type` is the type declared by the sender, falling back to
`application/octet-stream`. Attachment bytes are untrusted, so the
response is hardened against being rendered in a browser:
`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy:
default-src 'none'; sandbox`, and a `Content-Disposition: attachment`
filename. Do not undo those if you proxy this content to your own
users.

This response carries `X-Request-Id` but **not** the rate-limit headers;
the request is still metered.

A `404 not_found` here means one of: no such message, no such
attachment id on that message, or the stored bytes have already been
swept. The `detail` distinguishes them.

404.description:
No such message, no such attachment on that message, or the content
is no longer stored.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: No attachment `3` on message `9f2c1c1e-5f2a-4f0b-9f77-1f2a3b4c5d6e`.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: Attachment content is no longer available.

get.description:
Every address this account holds, with the plan's ceiling and how much
of it is used.

Reservations are per ACCOUNT, not per key: a reservation made with one
key is listed by every key on the same account, because the quota it
counts against is the account's.

Returns an empty list rather than a 404 when nothing is reserved, and
when reservations are unavailable on the environment.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description:
The full reserved address, including the domain. Percent-encode the
`@`. A bare local part is rejected with `422 invalid_request`.

delete.description:
Gives up the claim on an address, freeing a slot against
`plan.reservedAddresses`.

This does NOT delete a live mailbox on that address. The mailbox keeps
running and keeps receiving mail until its own expiry; releasing only
means the address is no longer held for you afterwards.

Scoped to the calling account. An address reserved by someone else is a
`404 not_found`, not a `403` — otherwise this endpoint would confirm
which addresses other customers hold.

404.description:
Not reserved by this account — or reservations are not configured on
this environment.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: `billing@allogebra.com` is not reserved by this account.

422.description: The address is missing, malformed, or has no domain.

value.title: Invalid request
value.detail: Provide the full address, including the domain.

post.description:
Queues one synthetic `message.received` event to a registered endpoint.

It takes the identical path through the queue, the signer and the
dispatcher's SSRF guard as a real delivery, so it proves your receiver
verifies signatures correctly *before* real mail depends on it. Because
the delivered payload is a pointer rather than message content (see the
`webhooks` section), no real message is needed to produce one.

Requires `plan.webhooks`. There is no endpoint for *registering* a
webhook — pass `webhookUrl` to `POST /v1/mailboxes` for that.

### Choosing the endpoint

Send `endpointId` to target a specific endpoint, or omit the body
entirely to use the most recently created endpoint on this key that is
not disabled. A malformed or absent body is treated as `{}`.

`endpointId` is scoped to the calling key: an id belonging to another
account resolves to nothing and returns `404 not_found`, the same as an
id that never existed.

### The event you will receive

- `type` is `message.received`, exactly as for real mail. There is no
  separate test event type — tell them apart by the `messageId`.
- `data.messageId` is prefixed `test_`, so it can never collide with a
  stored message id. `GET /v1/mailboxes/{address}/messages/{id}` on it
  returns `404 not_found`; there is nothing to fetch.
- `data.address` is `test@<current default domain>` and is not a real
  mailbox.
- Signature, `X-NTM-Delivery`, `User-Agent`, timeout and retry
  behaviour are identical to a real delivery.

### Asynchrony

`202` means queued, not delivered. Delivery happens in another Worker;
a failure here does not surface on this response. Check
`webhookEndpoints` on `GET /v1/me` if the event does not arrive — a
failed test attempt counts toward the auto-disable threshold like any
other.

This endpoint consumes a per-minute request, not daily mailbox quota.

value.note: Delivery is asynchronous. Check GET /v1/me for endpoint health if it does not arrive.

404.description:
No endpoint to test — none registered on this key, an `endpointId`
this key does not own, or webhooks are not configured on this
environment at all.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: No webhook endpoint is registered for this key. Register one by passing `webhookUrl` when you create a mailbox.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: Webhooks are not configured on this environment.

422.description:
The endpoint exists but is auto-disabled after repeated delivery
failures. Nothing will be sent to it until it is re-enabled, which
is a deliberate manual action — traffic alone never un-disables an
endpoint. Delete and re-register it, or contact support.

The signing secret for verifying deliveries is retrievable at any
time from `GET /dashboard/keys/{id}/webhook-secret` in the developer
portal — it is a verification secret, not a credential, so losing it
does not force you to rebuild the key.

value.title: Invalid request
value.detail: That endpoint is disabled after repeated delivery failures. See `webhookEndpoints` on GET /v1/me.

delete.description:
Deletes the endpoint. Deliveries stop immediately, including for
messages already queued: the dispatcher re-reads the destination from
the endpoint record at delivery time, so a job whose endpoint is gone is
discarded rather than sent.

Deletion is scoped to the calling key. An id belonging to another
account is a `404 not_found`, not a `403` — otherwise a guessed id would
be a way to silence someone else's deliveries.

Not idempotent: a second call returns `404 not_found`.

Mailboxes created with the deleted `webhookUrl` keep running and keep
receiving mail; they simply stop notifying you. Deleting an endpoint
does **not** delete its mailboxes, and re-registering the same URL later
creates a *new* endpoint id with a clean health record.

404.description:
No such endpoint on this key — or webhooks are not configured on
this environment.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: No webhook endpoint `whe_9fk2mqx7rp4lv9nb3tzc` for this key.

get.description:
Serves this specification as JSON. It is compiled from
`docs/api/openapi.yaml` at build time, so it is the same document you
are reading.

**Unauthenticated.** A developer needs to read the contract before they
have a key, and it contains nothing that is not already public. It is
also the one `/v1` route that is safe to cache: `Cache-Control: public,
max-age=300`, unlike the `no-store` on everything else.

Consequences of being outside the authenticated pipeline, all of which
are intentional:

- No `Authorization` header is required, and one sent is ignored.
- No metering: this call consumes no rate-limit or quota budget and the
  response carries no `X-RateLimit-*`, `X-Quota-*` or `X-Request-Id`
  headers.
- The origin guard does not run on this route, so a browser request
  reaches it — but no CORS headers are emitted either, so browser
  JavaScript still cannot read the response cross-origin.

4XX.description:
Not produced by this operation. It takes no parameters, requires no
credential, consumes no quota and reads no storage, so there is no
client error it can report; the only failure mode is a `500`.
Documented for tooling that requires a client-error response.

Other methods on this path are a different matter: they miss this
route entirely and fall through to the `/v1` catch-all, which
answers `403 origin_not_allowed` for `OPTIONS` and `404 not_found`
for anything else.

post.summary: Inbound mail arrived in one of your mailboxes
post.description:
Sent to the `webhookUrl` you registered on `POST /v1/mailboxes`, once
per message that mailbox accepts. This is the request **we make to
you** — implement it on your server, do not call it.

## The payload is a pointer, not the mail

The body carries `messageId`, `address` and `receivedAt` and nothing
else. No subject, no sender, no body, no verification codes. That is a
design decision, not an omission:

- **The `/v1` API stays the single source of truth for message
  content.** One shape to learn, one place that can be wrong, and a
  payload that cannot disagree with what you can fetch.
- **No message content ever crosses a third-party endpoint.** A
  callback URL can be mistyped, logged by an intermediary, proxied, or
  pointed at the wrong service. None of that leaks mail, because there
  is no mail in it. Reading the message needs your API key, which we
  never send anywhere.

So a handler looks like: verify the signature, enqueue the
`messageId`, return 200, then fetch
`GET /v1/mailboxes/{address}/messages/{messageId}` with your key out of
band.

## Request we send

```
POST <your webhookUrl>
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Accept: application/json
User-Agent: NowTempMail-Webhooks/1.0
X-NTM-Signature: t=1786097802,v1=7b53...
X-NTM-Delivery: 0f8d3b1a-6c2e-4a55-9d31-7b0c4e2f8a91
```

`User-Agent` is stable and is there so you can allowlist us and find us
in your access logs.

## Verifying `X-NTM-Signature`

The scheme is Stripe's, deliberately and almost byte-for-byte, so an
existing Stripe verifier works with the header name changed and nothing
else.

```
X-NTM-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<lowercase hex hmac-sha256>
signed payload  = `${t}.${rawBody}`
key             = your per-key webhook signing secret (whsec_...)
```

To verify:

1. Parse the header on `,` into `name=value` pairs. Read `t` and every
   `v1`. Tolerate extra schemes and whitespace — during a future digest
   migration a header may legitimately carry `t=..,v1=..,v2=..`.
2. Reject if `|now - t| > 300` seconds. Five minutes is the recommended
   tolerance and is what our own reference verifier defaults to. It
   bounds replay, and your clock skew has to fit inside it too.
3. Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, t + "." + rawBody)` as lowercase hex.
4. Compare against each `v1` value **in constant time**, and accept if
   any matches.

Three things people get wrong:

- **Sign the raw bytes.** Verify against the exact body string you
  received, before any JSON parse and re-serialise. We serialise once
  and sign and send that identical string; a round trip through your
  JSON library can change escaping and will break the digest.
- **The timestamp is inside the MAC**, not merely alongside it. That is
  what makes replay protection real: an attacker cannot re-present a
  captured body with a fresh `t`, because doing so invalidates the
  digest. Do not "simplify" the `t.body` separator away.
- **Compare in constant time.** A short-circuiting string compare leaks
  how many leading hex characters were right.

A reference verifier is published in the official Node SDK, which
exposes it as `verifyWebhook` from `nowtempmail/webhooks` — WebCrypto
only, so it runs unchanged on Node, Bun, Deno and edge runtimes.

`v1` is a version tag; when the digest changes, both `v1` and `v2` will
be emitted for a deprecation window.

## Idempotency

`X-NTM-Delivery` is the delivery id, and it is **stable across every
retry of the same message** — the same value is also `id` in the body.
Delivery is at-least-once; any queue eventually delivers twice. Dedupe
on this value and make your handler idempotent.

## What your endpoint must be

Enforced at registration *and* again at delivery — a hostname can
resolve differently between the two:

- `https` only. Not upgraded from `http`; `http` is rejected outright.
- Port 443 or 8443 only.
- No credentials in the URL (`https://user:pass@host/` is rejected).
- A public, multi-label DNS name. No raw IPv4 or IPv6 literals, no
  `localhost`, no `.local` / `.localhost` / `.internal` / `.intranet` /
  `.lan` / `.home.arpa` / `.corp` / `.private` suffix, and no
  wildcard-DNS host (`nip.io`, `sslip.io`, `xip.io`, `traefik.me`,
  `localtest.me`).

## Delivery behaviour

| | |
|---|---|
| Timeout | 10 seconds per attempt, hard |
| Redirects | **Not followed.** `redirect: manual` — a 3xx is a failed delivery |
| Success | Any 2xx. The response body is never read or logged |
| Retries | Queued with roughly exponential backoff and jitter, ceiling 5 minutes |
| Auto-disable | 20 consecutive failed **attempts** (retries count); any 2xx resets the streak |

**Respond 2xx fast, then do the work.** Return before you fetch the
message. Ten seconds is generous for "acknowledge and process
asynchronously"; an endpoint that accepts a connection and then stalls
burns its failure budget and walks itself to disabled.

A redirect is treated as a failure on purpose: following one would hand
the entire URL allowlist back to an attacker, since an innocent
`https://example.com/hook` could answer `302 Location:
http://169.254.169.254/…` and our egress would follow it. Register the
final URL.

Once an endpoint is disabled it receives nothing, and nothing re-enables
it on its own — traffic must never silently un-disable an endpoint. It
shows up as `status: "disabled"` in `webhookEndpoints` on
`GET /v1/me`, which is the only place that decision is visible.

## Rehearsing it

`POST /v1/webhooks/test` fires a synthetic event down the identical
path — same queue, same signer, same guard — so you can prove your
verifier works before real mail depends on it. Its `data.messageId` is
prefixed `test_` and has no message behind it.

requestBody.description: The signed event. Read the raw bytes before parsing.

parameters.name: X-NTM-Signature
parameters.description:
`t=<unix seconds>,v1=<lowercase hex hmac-sha256>`. The HMAC is over
`` `${t}.${rawBody}` `` keyed with your per-key signing secret.
Reject if `|now - t| > 300`.

parameters.name: X-NTM-Delivery
parameters.description:
Delivery id, stable across retries of the same message. Dedupe on
it. Same value as `id` in the body.

parameters.name: User-Agent
parameters.description: Always `NowTempMail-Webhooks/1.0`. Allowlist it if you need to.

200.description:
Acknowledged. Any 2xx counts and resets the endpoint's failure
streak. The response body is never read or logged — the status code
is the whole contract, so returning an empty body is fine.

400.description:
Any non-2xx — including a 3xx redirect, which is never followed —
is recorded as a failed attempt and the message is retried with
backoff. Twenty consecutive failed attempts disable the endpoint.

apiKey.description:
A NowTempMail developer API key, sent as an HTTP bearer credential:

```
Authorization: Bearer ntm_live_k7Rm2xQp9Ldv_4nT8wKmZqRv2sYbXdF6hJ3pLcN9gTuA5eW7yKxQ2
```

This is an API key, not an OAuth access token — it does not expire, it
is not refreshed, and it identifies an account rather than an end user.
The `bearer` scheme is used only as the transport.

### Format

`ntm_<environment>_<keyId>_<secret>`

| Segment | Value |
|---|---|
| `ntm` | Fixed prefix. |
| `<environment>` | `live` or `test`. |
| `<keyId>` | 12 characters. Public — safe to log, display and quote in support requests. |
| `<secret>` | 40 characters. Only ever stored as a SHA-256 hash and shown to you exactly once, at creation. |

Both variable segments are drawn from an alphabet with no look-alike
characters (no `0`, `1`, `l`, `I` or `O`), so a key read off a terminal
does not turn into a support ticket. A key that is truncated,
mistyped, or edited to change its environment segment returns
`invalid_key` — not a silent downgrade.

`ntm_test_` keys are metered against the **Free** plan limits whatever
the account is paying for, so load-testing a sandbox key cannot
accidentally run against Scale quotas. They are not a data sandbox:
mailboxes created with a test key are real and receive real mail.

### Never call this API from a browser

`/v1` emits no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and **rejects any request
that carries an `Origin` header** with `403 origin_not_allowed` — before
authentication, before metering. There is no allowlist to be added to.

This is deliberate. An API key in browser JavaScript is a published API
key: it is visible in the bundle, in devtools, and to every extension
the user has installed. Failing loudly here is better than a CORS error
a developer works around by proxying the key through their own frontend
anyway.

Call `/v1` from your server. If a browser needs the data, put your own
endpoint in front of it and keep the key server-side.

If your HTTP client sets `Origin` automatically (some do when following
redirects, or when configured for CORS-mode fetch in a non-browser
runtime), strip it.

MailboxAddress.name: address
MailboxAddress.description:
The full mailbox address, as returned by `POST /v1/mailboxes`.

Matched case-insensitively — the value is percent-decoded, trimmed and
lowercased before lookup. Percent-encoding the `@` (`%40`) is accepted
and recommended; a literal `@` in the path segment also works.

Two distinct `422 invalid_request` failures, both with
`parameter: "address"`:

- Malformed percent-encoding (`%zz`, a trailing `%`) — "The mailbox
  address is not correctly encoded."
- Decodes fine but is not a syntactically valid email address —
  "`<value>` is not a valid email address."

WebhookEndpointId.name: id
WebhookEndpointId.description:
A webhook endpoint id, as returned in `webhookEndpoints[].id` by
`GET /v1/me`. Of the form `whe_` plus 20 URL-safe characters. Opaque —
take it from `GET /v1/me`, do not construct it.

MessageId.name: messageId
MessageId.description: A message id from the list endpoint. A UUID.

AttachmentId.name: attachmentId
AttachmentId.description:
The attachment's index within the message, as a string (`"0"`, `"1"`,
…). Take it from the `attachments[].id` of the message or the
attachment list — do not construct it.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description:
Maximum number of messages to return. Default 25, maximum 100.

Out-of-range values are clamped rather than rejected: `0` and negatives
become 1, anything above 100 becomes 100, and a non-numeric value falls
back to the default of 25.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
The `nextCursor` from a previous page. Opaque — do not construct or
parse it. An undecodable value returns `422 invalid_request`.

XRequestId.name: X-Request-Id
XRequestId.description:
Your own correlation id. Echoed back on the response and written to the
server log. If omitted, one is generated in the form `req_<21 chars>`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests permitted per minute on this key's plan.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current minute window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description:
Epoch seconds at which the minute window resets and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`
returns to `X-RateLimit-Limit`. Fixed window, not sliding.

X-Quota-Limit.description: Mailbox creations permitted per UTC day on this key's plan.

X-Quota-Reset.description: Epoch seconds of the next 00:00 UTC boundary.

Retry-After.description:
Seconds to wait before retrying. On `rate_limit_exceeded` this is the
time to the next minute boundary; on `quota_exceeded` it is the time to
00:00 UTC, which can be most of a day.

X-Request-Id.description:
The request id — yours if you sent one, otherwise the generated one.
Also present as the `requestId` member of any error body.

Unauthorized.description:
No credential, an unusable credential, or a credential that is not a
developer API key.

| `code` | Cause |
|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | No `Authorization: Bearer` header, or a token that is not shaped like an API key (for example a mailbox JWT — `/v1` never accepts one). |
| `invalid_key` | Malformed, truncated, unknown, hand-edited, or wrong-secret key. |
| `key_revoked` | The key was revoked. Create a new one. |

These are produced before metering, so they carry no rate-limit
headers. A revoked key still costs you nothing in quota, but repeatedly
retrying one will not start working.

value.title: Authentication required
value.detail: Provide your API key as `Authorization: Bearer ntm_live_...`.

value.title: Authentication required
value.detail: This endpoint requires a developer API key, not a mailbox token.

value.title: Invalid API key
value.detail: The API key is not valid. Check for a truncated or mistyped key.

value.title: API key revoked
value.detail: This API key has been revoked. Create a new one in your dashboard.

Forbidden.description:
| `code` | Cause |
|---|---|
| `origin_not_allowed` | The request carried an `Origin` header, or it was an `OPTIONS` request. `/v1` is server-to-server only — see the security scheme. Checked before authentication, so this fires even without a key. |
| `account_suspended` | The account behind this key is suspended. |

Produced before metering; no rate-limit headers.

`OPTIONS` is answered this way on **every** `/v1` path, routed or not,
and the unrouted catch-all runs the same origin guard as a real route —
so a 404 can never be used to probe the API from a browser page.
Problems raised by the catch-all carry no `requestId`.

value.title: Browser origin not allowed
value.detail: The /v1 API does not accept browser requests. API keys must never be exposed to client-side code — call this API from your server instead.

preflight.summary: OPTIONS on any /v1 path — no requestId, this never reached the pipeline

value.title: Browser origin not allowed
value.detail: The /v1 API does not support CORS preflight. Call it from your server, not a browser.

value.title: Account suspended
value.detail: This account is suspended. Contact contact@nowtempmail.com.

PlanUpgradeRequired.description:
A paid capability was requested on a plan that does not include it. The
`parameter` member names the field where one applies, and `plan` is the
plan whose entitlement was checked. Compare against `plan` on
`GET /v1/me`.

Also returned when a *numeric* `ttlSeconds` fails validation for any
reason, including being malformed rather than over the ceiling — see
`POST /v1/mailboxes`.

Nothing was created. Retrying without the offending field succeeds; the
request still consumed a per-minute slot, and on `POST /v1/mailboxes`
it consumed daily mailbox quota too, because metering runs before
validation.

value.title: Plan upgrade required
value.detail: Custom addresses require a paid plan. Your key is on Free.

value.title: Plan upgrade required
value.detail: `ttlSeconds` of 2592000 exceeds the Starter plan maximum of 604800. Upgrade your plan for longer-lived mailboxes.

ttlTooSmall.summary: A numeric ttlSeconds that is merely malformed still yields 402

value.title: Plan upgrade required
value.detail: `ttlSeconds` must be at least 300 (5 minutes).

value.title: Plan upgrade required
value.detail: Webhooks require a paid plan. Your key is on Free.

value.title: Plan upgrade required
value.detail: Your Starter plan allows 5 reserved addresses and you are using 5. Release one first.

AddressConflict.description:
The requested `address` is not available. A live mailbox on that address
and a reservation held by another account produce the identical body —
distinguishing them would let you enumerate other customers' held
addresses.

Reservations are checked before mailboxes, because a reservation
outlives the mailbox and is the stronger claim.

Note `address_reserved` (409) is defined in the error vocabulary but is
not emitted by any endpoint in this release: a *reserved word* such as
`admin` comes back as `422 invalid_request`, and a name held by another
account comes back as `address_taken` below.

value.title: Address already in use
value.detail: `my-signup-test@allogebra.com` is not available.

value.title: Address already in use
value.detail: That address was just taken.

MailboxNotFound.description:
No such mailbox — or one this key does not own, or one that has expired.
These are intentionally indistinguishable.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: No mailbox `crystal482@allogebra.com`.

MessageNotFound.description:
No such message in that mailbox — or the mailbox itself is not visible
to this key.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: No message `9f2c1c1e-5f2a-4f0b-9f77-1f2a3b4c5d6e` in mailbox `crystal482@allogebra.com`.

value.title: Not found
value.detail: No mailbox `crystal482@allogebra.com`.

InvalidAddress.description:
The `address` path segment is not usable: either its percent-encoding is
malformed, or it does not decode to a syntactically valid email address.

Malformed encoding is a **422, not a 500** — `%zz` is a client error and
is reported as one.

value.title: Invalid request
value.detail: `not-an-address` is not a valid email address.

value.title: Invalid request
value.detail: The mailbox address is not correctly encoded.

TooManyRequests.description:
The per-minute request limit for this key's plan was exceeded
(`rate_limit_exceeded`). Wait `Retry-After` seconds — or until
`X-RateLimit-Reset` — and retry.

`quota_exceeded` is possible only on `POST /v1/mailboxes`.

No `X-Request-Id` response header here — read `requestId` off the body.

value.title: Rate limit exceeded
value.detail: You have exceeded 30 requests per minute on the Free plan.

InternalError.description:
Something failed on our side, or quota metering was unavailable and the
request was refused rather than served unmetered. Nothing internal is
echoed back. Safe to retry with backoff; quote `requestId` if it
persists.

value.title: Internal server error
value.detail: The request could not be completed.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 problem document. Served as
`application/problem+json; charset=utf-8`.

Branch on `code`, never on `detail` or on the HTTP status alone —
several codes share a status. `code` values are stable and are never
renamed in place.

### Every code

| `code` | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | 401 | No credential, or a credential that is not a developer API key. |
| `invalid_key` | 401 | The key is malformed, unknown, or the secret does not match. |
| `key_revoked` | 401 | The key was revoked. |
| `account_suspended` | 403 | The owning account is suspended. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | Reserved. Not emitted by any endpoint in this release. |
| `origin_not_allowed` | 403 | The request carried a browser `Origin` header, or it was an `OPTIONS` request. |
| `plan_upgrade_required` | 402 | A paid capability (`address`, `reserve`, `ttlSeconds` above the plan ceiling, `webhookUrl`) was requested on a plan without it, or a reserved-address allowance was exhausted. |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such mailbox, message, attachment or webhook endpoint — or one this key cannot see. Also the unrouted-path response. |
| `address_taken` | 409 | The requested `address` is already a live mailbox, or is reserved by another account. |
| `address_reserved` | 409 | Defined but **not emitted** by any endpoint in this release. A reserved word returns `invalid_request`; a name held by someone else returns `address_taken`. |
| `invalid_request` | 422 | A parameter is malformed, unusable, or reserved. |
| `rate_limit_exceeded` | 429 | Per-minute request limit exceeded. |
| `quota_exceeded` | 429 | Daily mailbox quota exhausted. Only from `POST /v1/mailboxes`. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | Server-side failure. |

`requestId` is present on every problem raised inside the authenticated
pipeline. It is **absent** on problems from the unrouted catch-all
(`not_found` for an unknown path, and `origin_not_allowed` for
`OPTIONS`), which never enter it.

type.description:
A documentation URL for this error, of the form
`https://nowtempmail.com/developers/errors#<code>`. Dereferenceable
for a human; do not parse it — use `code`.

code.description:
The stable machine-readable identifier. This is the field to branch
on. Duplicated out of `type` so callers do not have to parse a URL.

title.description: Fixed human-readable summary for the code.

status.description: The HTTP status code. Always matches the response status.

detail.description:
Human-readable explanation of this particular occurrence. **Not**
part of the contract — wording changes without notice.
detail.example: Custom addresses are not available yet on this API version.

requestId.description:
Correlation id for this request. Present on every problem generated
after the request enters the `/v1` pipeline. Quote it in support
requests.

parameter.description:
Extension member. Names the offending request field when one can be
identified — `address`, `domain`, `ttlSeconds`, `reserve`,
`webhookUrl` or `cursor`. Present on `invalid_request`,
`plan_upgrade_required` and `address_taken`.

plan.description:
Extension member. The plan whose ceiling or entitlement was hit.
Present on `plan_upgrade_required`, `rate_limit_exceeded`,
`quota_exceeded`, and on `POST /v1/mailboxes` address failures.

maxTtlSeconds.description:
Extension member. On any `ttlSeconds` failure, the ceiling for the
calling key's plan.

endpointId.description:
Extension member. On `POST /v1/webhooks/test` against a disabled
endpoint, which endpoint was refused.

paywall.description:
Whether paid plans are being sold yet. While `enabled` is `false`,
every account receives the launch plan's capabilities regardless of
what it pays, so BRANCH ON THIS rather than inferring a tier from
the key prefix or the account's stored plan.

subscription.description:
The account's subscription, or `null` for an account that has never
subscribed. Exposed so an integration can see a renewal or
cancellation coming without opening the dashboard.

keyId.description: The public 12-character id of the calling key. Safe to log.

environment.description:
Which key form was presented. `test` keys are metered against the
Free plan whatever the account's actual plan is, so `plan` below
will read `free` for a test key on a paid account.

webhookEndpoints.description:
Every webhook endpoint registered against this key, newest first,
with its delivery health. Empty on a key that has never passed
`webhookUrl` to `POST /v1/mailboxes`, and on an environment with no
developer database bound.

WebhookEndpoint.title: WebhookEndpoint
WebhookEndpoint.description:
One registered callback URL and its delivery health. Endpoints are
created as a side effect of `POST /v1/mailboxes` with `webhookUrl`, are
deduplicated by URL per key, and are removed with
`DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}`.

url.description:
The destination, normalised by the WHATWG URL parser at
registration. This is what deliveries are POSTed to — it is re-read
at delivery time, so an endpoint you delete stops receiving even
already-queued messages.

status.description:
`disabled` once 20 consecutive delivery **attempts** have failed —
queue retries count. A disabled endpoint receives nothing at all,
and `POST /v1/webhooks/test` against it returns
`422 invalid_request`. Nothing re-enables it automatically;
traffic alone must never un-disable an endpoint.

consecutiveFailures.description:
Failed attempts since the last success. Any 2xx resets it to `0`.
Auto-disable trips at 20.

lastSuccessAt.description: Epoch seconds of the last 2xx, or `null` if there has never been one.

lastFailureAt.description: Epoch seconds of the last failed attempt, or `null`.

disabledAt.description: Epoch seconds at which auto-disable tripped, or `null` while active.

disabledReason.description:
Why it was disabled, or `null` while active. Of the form
`auto_disabled_after_20_failures:<last reason>`, where the last
reason is `http_<status>`, `timeout`, `network_error`, or
`url_rejected_<guard reason>` (the callback URL stopped passing the
SSRF guard — for example its DNS name started resolving somewhere
we refuse to POST).

Plan.title: Plan
Plan.description:
The limits attached to this key. The full tier table:

| | Free | Starter | Scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requestsPerMinute` | 30 | 300 | 1200 |
| `mailboxesPerDay` | 50 | 2,000 | 25,000 |
| `customAddress` | false | true | true |
| `reservedAddresses` | 0 | 5 | 100 |
| `maxTtlSeconds` | 86,400 (24h) | 604,800 (7d) | 2,592,000 (30d) |
| `webhooks` | false | true | true |

Every field here is enforced. Asking for a capability your plan does not
include returns `402 plan_upgrade_required` rather than being ignored.

A `ntm_test_` key is metered against **Free** limits whatever the account
is paying, so you can exercise rate-limit handling without spending your
live budget.

While checkout is switched off (`paywall.enabled: false` on
`GET /v1/me`), both environments share the launch limits — the test
pinning takes effect when billing goes live. Read the plan from
`GET /v1/me` rather than assuming it from the key prefix.

requestsPerMinute.description: Burst ceiling across all `/v1` endpoints, per rolling minute window.

mailboxesPerDay.description: Mailbox creations permitted per UTC day.

maxTtlSeconds.description:
The ceiling for a caller-supplied `ttlSeconds` on
`POST /v1/mailboxes`. This is what you may *ask* for — the default
when you omit `ttlSeconds` is 86,400 on every plan, including the
ones whose ceiling is higher.

customAddress.description:
Whether this plan may choose its own local part via `address` on
`POST /v1/mailboxes`. `false` makes that field a
`402 plan_upgrade_required`.

reservedAddresses.description:
How many local parts the account may hold across mailbox expiry via
`reserve: true`. Compare with `usage.reservedAddressesUsed`. `0`
means `reserve` is unavailable on this plan.

webhooks.description:
Whether this plan may register an inbound-mail webhook via
`webhookUrl` on `POST /v1/mailboxes`, and use
`POST /v1/webhooks/test`. `false` makes both a
`402 plan_upgrade_required`.

requestsThisMinute.description:
Requests consumed in the current minute window, excluding this
`GET /v1/me` call — which is metered in peek mode and consumes
nothing.

reservedAddressesUsed.description:
Address reservations currently held. Counted per **account**, not
per key, so every key on the account sees the same number and they
share one allowance from `plan.reservedAddresses`. `0` on an
environment with no developer database bound.

minute.description: Epoch seconds at which the minute window resets.

day.description: Epoch seconds of the next 00:00 UTC boundary.

default.description:
True for the single domain `POST /v1/mailboxes` will currently
choose. Which domain that is changes as the rotation logic
weighs domain health and usage.

CreateMailboxRequest.title: CreateMailboxRequest
CreateMailboxRequest.description:
Every member is optional, and **an explicit `null` is treated as "not
provided"** for all of them — `{"address": null}` behaves identically to
`{}`. Sending `null` is never an error and never clears anything.

See the endpoint description for the full validation rules, the
evasion-aware reserved-word check, and the order fields are validated
in.

address.description:
The desired local part (`my-signup-test`) or a full address
(`my-signup-test@allogebra.com`, whose domain half is discarded).
Trimmed and lowercased; 3–64 characters matching
`^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9._-]*[a-z0-9])?$`, no `..`, not a reserved name.

Requires `plan.customAddress` (Starter, Scale) —
`402 plan_upgrade_required` otherwise.

`null` means "not provided": you get a generated address.

domain.description:
Which domain to create the address on. Must be one that
`GET /v1/domains` currently lists; trimmed and lowercased first.
Not plan-gated. Omit it, or send `null`, and the rotation logic
chooses.

ttlSeconds.description:
Mailbox lifetime in seconds. Whole number, minimum `300`, maximum
`plan.maxTtlSeconds`. Rejected rather than clamped.

**Default 86,400 (24 hours) on every plan** when omitted or `null`,
including plans whose ceiling is higher.

reserve.description:
Hold the local part for your account beyond this mailbox's expiry.
Requires `address` — `true` on its own is `422 invalid_request`.
Counts against `plan.reservedAddresses`.

Only the literal boolean `true` has any effect; any other value,
including the string `"true"` and `null`, is silently treated as
`false`.

webhookUrl.description:
HTTPS endpoint POSTed a signed `message.received` event for every
message this mailbox accepts. Must pass the SSRF guard: https, port
443 or 8443, no credentials, public multi-label DNS name.

Requires `plan.webhooks` (Starter, Scale). Registering the same URL
twice on one key reuses the existing endpoint. `null` means "not
provided" — it does not detach anything.

address.description:
The address. Always lowercase. Generated addresses are a
ten-character local part of a word plus digits; a custom address is
the local part you asked for, trimmed and lowercased.

domain.description:
The domain actually used — your `domain` if you sent one, otherwise
the rotation logic's choice. Never the domain half of an `address`
you sent, which is discarded.

ttlSeconds.description:
The lifetime granted. Equal to the `ttlSeconds` you sent, or 86,400
when you sent none.

reserved.description:
Whether the local part is now held for your account across expiry.
`true` only when you sent `reserve: true` and the reservation
succeeded.

webhookUrl.description:
The registered callback, WHATWG-normalised — which may differ from
what you sent. `null` when no webhook is attached to this mailbox.
The endpoint id is not returned here; read it from
`webhookEndpoints` on `GET /v1/me`.

expiresAt.description:
Epoch seconds. Past this point the mailbox and its messages are gone
and every endpoint under it returns `404 not_found`.

messageCount.description:
Messages received, as counted on the mailbox record. This is a
best-effort counter maintained by the mail receiver and can drift
from the length of the message list under concurrent delivery. Use
the list endpoint when the exact set matters.

lastMessageAt.description: Epoch seconds of the most recent delivery, or `null` if none.

deletedMessages.description: How many messages were removed along with the mailbox.

nextCursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` when `hasMore` is
`false`. Opaque.

from.description:
The envelope sender as received, often in `Display Name <addr>`
form. Not normalised and not verified — treat it as untrusted text.

subject.description: `(no subject)` when the message carried none.

verificationCodes.description:
Verification codes extracted from the message at ingest — the
reason most callers never need to fetch a body.

Extraction looks for 4–8 digit numeric codes and 6–10 character
uppercase alphanumeric codes containing at least one digit, within
200 characters of a word like *code*, *otp*, *verify*, *passcode* or
*authentication*. It is a heuristic: it can return more than one
candidate, and a message can legitimately contain none. When
several are returned they are in no meaningful order — if you need
certainty, match against the message body yourself.

Empty array when nothing matched.

to.description:
The mailbox this message was read from — the decoded, lowercased
`address` path segment, which is also the address this request was
authorised against. It is not read from the message headers, so it
never reflects a `Bcc:` or an alias the sender used.

subject.description: `(no subject)` when the message carried none.

receivedAt.description: Epoch seconds, or `null` if the stored record has no timestamp.

text.description:
Plain-text body. Falls back to the raw HTML source when the message
carried no `text/plain` part, and is an empty string when it carried
neither. `null` only for records stored before this field existed.

**Untrusted**, and not guaranteed to be plain text — see the
fallback above.

html.description:
HTML body as received, or `null` if the message had none.
**Untrusted.** Never inject it into a page without sandboxing and
sanitising it.

verificationCodes.description:
Extracted verification codes — the same set the list endpoint
returns for this message, produced by the same ingest-time
extraction. Empty array when nothing matched. See
`MessageSummary.verificationCodes` for what the heuristic does and
does not guarantee.

id.description:
The attachment's index within the message, as a string. Unique
within a message only.

filename.description:
Sender-supplied filename, falling back to `attachment_<index>`.
**Untrusted** — sanitise before using it as a path.

contentType.description:
Sender-declared MIME type, falling back to
`application/octet-stream`. Not verified against the bytes.

WebhookTestRequest.title: WebhookTestRequest
WebhookTestRequest.description:
Optional. Omit the body entirely — or send `{}`, or anything that is not
valid JSON — to target the most recently created endpoint on this key
that is not disabled.

endpointId.description:
Which endpoint to test, from `webhookEndpoints[].id` on
`GET /v1/me`. Scoped to the calling key: an id you do not own is a
`404 not_found`, indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

Unlike the default selection, an explicit `endpointId` will find a
**disabled** endpoint — which is then refused with
`422 invalid_request`, so you get told why rather than silently
testing something else.

queued.description: Always `true`. A failure to queue is an error response, not `false`.

endpointId.description: The endpoint the event was queued for.

url.description: Where it will be delivered, as recorded on the endpoint.

messageId.description:
The `data.messageId` your receiver will see. Always prefixed
`test_`, so it can never collide with a real message id — and so a
receiver can tell a drill from real mail. There is no message behind
it; fetching it returns `404 not_found`.

note.description: Fixed human-readable reminder that delivery is asynchronous.
note.example: Delivery is asynchronous. Check GET /v1/me for endpoint health if it does not arrive.

WebhookEvent.title: WebhookEvent
WebhookEvent.description:
The JSON body POSTed to your endpoint, and the exact bytes the
`X-NTM-Signature` HMAC is taken over.

**This is a pointer, not the message.** It carries no subject, no
sender, no body and no verification codes. Two reasons, both
deliberate:

1. The `/v1` API stays the single source of truth for what is in a
   message. One shape to learn, one place that can be wrong, and a
   payload that cannot go stale relative to what you can fetch.
2. No message content ever crosses a third-party endpoint. A callback
   URL can be mistyped, logged by an intermediary, proxied, or simply
   handed to the wrong service — and none of that leaks mail, because
   there is no mail in it. Reading the message requires your API key,
   which we never send anywhere.

So the flow is: receive event, verify signature, then
`GET /v1/mailboxes/{data.address}/messages/{data.messageId}` with your
key.

The object is additive-only. Treat unknown members as forward
compatibility, not as an error.

id.description:
Delivery id. **Identical to the `X-NTM-Delivery` header and stable
across every retry of the same message** — this is the value to
dedupe on. Delivery is at-least-once; any queue eventually delivers
twice.

type.description:
One value today. The field exists so you can `switch` on it without
rewriting your handler when a second event type ships — reject
anything you do not recognise rather than assuming.

A `POST /v1/webhooks/test` event also has type `message.received`;
identify it by the `test_` prefix on `data.messageId`.

createdAt.description:
Epoch seconds, and the same value as the `t=` component inside
`X-NTM-Signature`.

messageId.description:
The message id to fetch. Pass it to
`GET /v1/mailboxes/{address}/messages/{id}`.

receivedAt.description:
Unix **milliseconds** — when the mail was accepted. Note the
unit: `createdAt` above and every timestamp in the REST API are
seconds, this one is not.
